intuition: Start from an unvisited vertex and follow every reachable edge. All vertices found belong to one connected group. Mark them so the next scan does not count that group again. Repeat from each remaining unvisited vertex, including isolated vertices with no edges.

Build an adjacency list in both directions for every undirected edge. Then scan every vertex label, not merely the labels occurring in edges. An unvisited vertex identifies a new component, even when it has no neighbors. Increase the count and use an explicit stack to visit everything reachable from that start.

Mark a neighbor when it is discovered and pushed, rather than waiting until it is popped. A cycle or multiple incoming routes could otherwise put the same vertex on the stack several times. Once a traversal finishes, all vertices in that component are marked; later outer-loop visits skip them. The number of traversal starts is consequently the number of components.
This reasoning includes isolated vertices naturally and does not depend on the graph being acyclic.

steps: For n=5 and edges [[0,1],[1,2],[3,4]], build neighbors 0↔1↔2 and 3↔4.
The outer scan reaches unvisited vertex 0. Count the first component and place 0 on the stack.
Exploration discovers 1, then 2, marking both at discovery. The visited set becomes {0,1,2}.
The outer scan skips 1 and 2, then starts a new traversal at 3, discovering 4.
All five vertices are now visited and exactly two traversals were started. Return 2.

codeNotes.note: Every input edge is undirected, so reachability must include its reverse direction as well as the forward one.
Only a previously unvisited start increments the count; the entire ensuing traversal belongs to that one component.
Discovery-time marking prevents cycles and shared routes from scheduling duplicate visits.

keyDecision: Increase the group count once per new traversal, not once per vertex visited.

concept.question: How can one exploration identify a whole connected component?
intuition: Testing every pair of vertices for connectivity repeats the same routes. Once an exploration reaches all vertices connected to one starting vertex, they form a complete component.
Choose any still-unvisited vertex and follow all its connections until no new vertex is reachable. Mark that whole group, count one component, then start again from another unvisited vertex.
concept.observation: Start a new component only from a vertex no earlier exploration reached.
approach: Build neighbor lists for all vertices, including isolated ones.
Explore every newly found vertex’s neighbors and mark discoveries.
Count one component per exploration started from an unvisited vertex.
concept.correctness: Following all neighbors reaches every vertex connected to the start, and never crosses into a disconnected group because no connecting route exists. Starting again only at unseen vertices produces disjoint exhaustive groups, so the number of starts equals the number of connected components.

complexity.explanation: Each vertex is discovered once and each undirected edge is examined from both ends. Work and neighbor-list storage are proportional to vertices plus edges.

pitfalls: Start a new component only from a vertex no earlier exploration reached.
Do not omit vertices just because they have no edge.
